```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(stream)
set.seed(1000)
```

In an evolving stream, the distribution of incoming points changes over time.
A clustering model needs to forget outdated observations to follow this concept
drift. This guide adapts the moving-cluster and evolving-stream comparison
examples from the package's original `stream_vignette.Rnw`.

## Inspect moving clusters

`DSD_Benchmark(1)` generates two clusters that move diagonally across the unit
square and intersect in the middle, together with background noise.

```{r benchmark}
stream <- DSD_Benchmark(1)
stream
```

Plot four short sections of the stream, skipping 1400 points between plots.
Fixed axis limits make the movement visible. Both `plot()` and `get_points()`
advance the stream.

```{r snapshots, fig.height=7}
local({
  old_par <- par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
  on.exit(par(old_par))
  for (i in seq_len(4)) {
    plot(stream, n = 250, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1),
      main = paste("Starting at point", 1 + (i - 1) * 1650))
    arrows(0.15, 0.85, 0.85, 0.15, col = "gray70", lwd = 2)
    arrows(0.15, 0.15, 0.85, 0.85, col = "gray70", lwd = 2)
    if (i < 4) invisible(get_points(stream, n = 1400))
  }
})
```

The arrows indicate the directions of travel. Near the crossing, the two
generating clusters overlap, making them difficult to distinguish using only
the observed features.

## Compare models on the same points

Generate and store 5000 points. Resetting a `DSD_Memory` stream replays the same
points, which makes comparisons fair. Resetting a generator resets its position
but does not in general reproduce the same random observations.

```{r fixed-stream}
set.seed(0)
stream <- DSD_Memory(DSD_Benchmark(1), n = 5000)
```

Compare a sample biased toward recent data, a fading sliding window, D-Stream,
and DBSTREAM. The sample and window use k-means to form two macro-clusters.
D-Stream and DBSTREAM determine macro-clusters using their built-in methods.
We use `lambda = 0.01` for the window and density-based methods to forget older
points quickly enough to follow the movement.

```{r models}
algorithms <- list(
  "Sample + k-means" = DSC_TwoStage(
    micro = DSC_Sample(k = 100, biased = TRUE),
    macro = DSC_Kmeans(k = 2)),
  "Window + k-means" = DSC_TwoStage(
    micro = DSC_Window(horizon = 100, lambda = 0.01),
    macro = DSC_Kmeans(k = 2)),
  "D-Stream" = DSC_DStream(gridsize = 0.1, lambda = 0.01),
  "DBSTREAM" = DSC_DBSTREAM(r = 0.05, lambda = 0.01)
)
```

`evaluate_stream()` uses prequential evaluation: it evaluates the current model
on the next batch, then updates the model with those points. Here each batch
contains 100 points, producing 50 evaluations per model. The adjusted Rand
index (`crand`) compares the macro-clustering with the true cluster labels.
Assignments go through micro-clusters to retain the shape of density-based
macro-clusters.

```{r evaluation}
evaluation <- lapply(algorithms, function(model) {
  reset_stream(stream)
  evaluate_stream(model, stream, horizon = 100, n = 5000,
    measure = "crand", type = "macro", assign = "micro")
})
scores <- sapply(evaluation, function(x) x[, "crand"])
head(scores)
```

The first score is `NA` because each model starts empty. Plot the scores over
time and compare their distributions over the stream.

```{r score-trajectories}
position <- evaluation[[1]][, "points"]
matplot(position, scores, type = "l", lwd = 1,
  xlab = "Points processed", ylab = "Adjusted Rand index")
legend("bottomleft", legend = names(algorithms),
  col = seq_along(algorithms), lty = seq_along(algorithms), cex = 0.8)
```

```{r score-distributions}
boxplot(scores, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.8, ylab = "Adjusted Rand index")
```

Read the score trajectories alongside the snapshots: overlap can lower quality
even when a model follows the movement. The methods also differ in their noise
handling; k-means assigns points to a cluster, while the density-based methods
can leave points unassigned. These settings illustrate one experiment rather
than establishing a ranking across streams.

## Animate the stream and clustering

The following animation shows 5000 points in batches of 100, with DBSTREAM's
micro- and macro-clusters overlaid. The GIF loops automatically, displaying ten
frames per second. It is embedded directly in the HTML, so the document can be
shared without separate image files.

Knitr creates the GIF using the `gifski` R package; FFmpeg is not required.
Install `gifski` before rendering to include the animation. The animation chunk
is skipped when `gifski` is unavailable or the output is not HTML.

```{r moving-animation, eval=knitr::is_html_output() && requireNamespace("gifski", quietly=TRUE), fig.show='animate', animation.hook='gifski', interval=0.1, aniopts='loop', dev='png', fig.width=6.4, fig.height=4.8, dpi=100, fig.retina=1, fig.alt='DBSTREAM following two moving clusters'}
local({
  set.seed(1000)
  animation_stream <- DSD_Benchmark(1)
  animation_model <- DSC_DBSTREAM(r = 0.05, lambda = 0.01)
  for (i in seq_len(50)) {
    batch <- get_points(animation_stream, n = 100)
    update(animation_model, batch)
    plot(animation_model, remove_info(batch), type = "both",
      xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1),
      main = paste("DBSTREAM after", i * 100, "points"))
  }
})
```

For interactive exploration, the following examples use the package's animation
helpers. They are not run when building the vignette. Start with a fresh stream
and model.

```{r animations, eval=FALSE}
stream <- DSD_Benchmark(1)
animate_data(stream, n = 5000, horizon = 100,
  xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1))

stream <- DSD_Benchmark(1)
model <- DSC_DBSTREAM(r = 0.05, lambda = 0.01)
animate_cluster(model, stream, n = 5000, horizon = 100,
  measure = "crand", type = "macro", assign = "micro",
  plot.args = list(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), type = "both"))
```
